data.title: Foreign investors post biggest Japanese stock selloff in nine weeks as AI jitters deepen
data.description:
Foreign investors made their biggest Japanese equity sales in nine weeks in the week ended November 20, as a wider selloff in global AI-linked companies and hawkish comments from US Federal Reserve officials weighed on risk appetite.

They withdrew a net 571.6 billion yen ($3.59 billion) from local stocks, the largest amount for a week since September 19, Ministry of Finance data showed on Friday.

The Nikkei 225 fell 7.7% last week, closing at a seven-month low of 56,436.65. This week, the Nikkei has gained about 3.7% so far.

Global AI-related stocks have come under pressure this month due to concerns about returns on massive investments in the AI buildout as well as the prospect of tighter AI regulation and oversight after Democrats won the US midterm elections.

While the outflows trimmed foreign investors' net purchases of Japanese stocks to 9.99 trillion yen so far this year, they are higher than their net purchases of about 7.64 trillion yen in the same period last year.

Foreigners also bought a net 208.5 billion yen of Japanese long-term bonds, marking an eighth consecutive week of net purchases. They sold a net 1.79 trillion yen of short-term bills.

Meanwhile, Japanese investors bought a net 423.5 billion yen of foreign long-term bonds, ending a two-week streak of net selling. They also purchased a net 15.8 billion yen of short-term bills.

Japanese investors sold a net 350.8 billion yen of overseas equities, reversing nearly all of the 363.1 billion yen in net purchases recorded the previous week.

($1 = 159.2800 yen)

data.title: Conservatives would win election in Australia's second state, says poll
data.description:
Australia's centre-right conservatives look set for a decisive win at an election in the state of Victoria on Saturday, a new poll showed, ending more than a decade of state Labor government and seeing off populist right-wing challengers.

An election result in line with the poll in the country's second-most populous state would reassure establishment parties that a surge in support for Pauline Hanson's One Nation, Australia's answer to US President Donald Trump, Alternative for Germany and Reform UK, does not translate to votes at scale.

The Newspoll published on Friday said the Liberal-National coalition led by Jess Wilson, 36, came in ahead of Labor 57.5% to 42.5% when counting for likely voter preferences. That would hand the conservatives up to 67 of the state's 88 lower house seats, the poll said.

If that pattern is repeated at the ballot, the Victorian Labor party would win just 17 seats, from 54 currently, the poll showed, which would be the party's worst showing on record.

A conservative win would close the book on a government which rode high in the polls for years — even through some of the world's longest COVID lockdowns, in its capital city Melbourne — but which has become deeply unpopular as voters fret over worsening affordability and new taxes intended to pay down the highest state debt in the country.

It would also sound the alarm for Labor governments in larger New South Wales state, which faces an election in March, and federally, where an election is due by 2028.

One Nation was formed by maverick Hanson in 1997 on an anti-immigration platform and remained at the political fringes until May 2025, when a resounding defeat in a national election threw the federal conservative coalition into crisis. Hanson's party won just 6% of the vote at that election but by year-end was leading some polls.

This May, the party won its first federal lower house seat in a byelection, in a regional New South Wales seat that borders Victoria. The party ran just five lower house candidates in Victoria in 2022, winning none, but has run candidates in all 88 seats in 2026.

Under Australia's preferential ballot system, if no candidate wins a majority, the contender with the lowest count is eliminated and their votes are distributed to the person their supporters nominated as their next preference.

data.title: Malaysia's Large-Cap Contractors Likely Insulated From Nvidia Shipment Halt — Market Talk
data.description: Malaysia's large-cap contractors should be relatively insulated from the impact of Nvidia's reported halt on server shipments to Southeast Asia, given their data center exposure is weighted toward U.S. hyperscalers, Citi analyst Steven Chan says in a note. He sees no delays to existing projects but flags potential risks to future tenders from 2H 2027 onward. Non-hyperscaler customers, including cloud providers and colocation operators, are likely to be more affected by Nvidia's move, he adds. Chan remains cautious on the broader data center sector, as China-linked demand accounts for a significant share of capacity and future projects. Operators and contractors outside the U.S. hyperscaler ecosystem could face risks of slower project conversion, tighter financing and pressured valuations, Citi adds. (yingxian.wong@wsj.com)

data.title: Indian shares muted as IT pullback offsets broader gains
data.description:
By Bharath Rajeswaran and Vivek Kumar M

Indian shares slipped marginally on Friday, as IT stocks dropped after a four-session rally to offset broader gains from returning foreign inflows.

The Nifty 50 slipped 0.16% to 25,845.1 while the Sensex eased 0.29% to 84,077.8, as of 10:03 a.m. IST.

Eleven of the 16 major sectors logged gains. The broader small-caps and mid-caps gained about 1% each.

The 50-stock Nifty index and the Sensex are up 0.2% each so far this week, consolidating after a nearly 15% surge over the last four weeks that saw Indian benchmarks outperforming Asian and emerging market peers.

The rally in November was driven by record monthly foreign inflows, worth $15.5 billion, aided by a global AI trade reversal and robust earnings.

Brent crude futures hovered around $96.5 per barrel, rising 4.2% over the week as ongoing attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and Saudi energy infrastructure heightened concerns over oil exports from the conflict-hit region.

"The rise in Brent crude is negative news in the context of rising inflation in India, while the US tariff proposal is another threat," said VK Vijayakumar, chief investment strategist at Geojit Investments.

After the recent rally, "a consolidation phase appears likely in the near term," Vijayakumar said.

IT index fell 1.5% after rising 8% in the last four sessions.

Among stocks, Waaree Renewable Technologies surged 10% after receiving a letter of award for a 120 MWp turnkey EPC project.

Freight wagon manufacturer Texmaco Rail gained 2.6% on winning an order worth $6.02 million from Utkal Alumina International for supply of 108 railway wagons.

Engineering, procurement and construction firm EMS added 2% on securing a $2.8 million order from the National Highways Authority of India.

Coal India unit Mahanadi Coalfields (MHAN.NS) fell 1.5% in its trading debutk.

Jet Freight Logistics fell 2% after the logistics firm said India's markets regulator summoned its chairman and managing director as part of an ongoing investigation into the company.

data.title: Trump says Huang is excited about his 'second term' at Nvidia
data.description:
President Donald Trump said Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is happy to return to the role, calling it his “second term,” as the president again defended his intervention in the executive’s reinstatement despite bipartisan national security concerns.

Speaking to reporters at Mar-a-Lago on Thursday, Trump said he had not spoken to Huang since Nvidia announced his return but added, “When I did speak to him, he is so happy to be going back. He calls it his second term.”

Trump dismissed concerns surrounding Huang’s reinstatement, saying, “Based on information and belief, I think he’s absolutely fine.” Asked what information he had, Trump offered no specifics, saying only, “The information I have, which is a lot of information.”

Trump had pushed Nvidia’s board to reinstate Huang and enlisted Vice President JD Vance to make a personal appeal. The move drew criticism from both parties, with lawmakers calling for scrutiny of Huang’s ties to the administration. Huang is scheduled to testify privately before House lawmakers on Dec. 1 and publicly before the Senate on Dec. 3.

Nvidia shares surged more than 31% on Monday following the announcement but fell more than 9.5% over the next two sessions. Trump said, “I will tell you, the market feels very good about it,” adding that he believed he had done “a great thing for our country and even for the world.”

Trump is scheduled to attend a groundbreaking event for Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing chip plant expansion in Arizona on Dec. 4. Asked whether Huang might join him, Trump said, “I would be glad to take him.”

data.title: India bonds decline ahead of fresh debt sale as elevated oil prices fan inflation worries
data.description:
By Dharamraj Dhutia

Indian government bonds tumbled in early deals on Friday, pinched by higher oil prices one week before the central bank's monetary policy decision, while investors also remained cautious in the face of large fresh debt supply through the weekly auction.

The benchmark 6.94% 2036 bond (IN069436G=CC) yield traded at 7.2696% as of 10 a.m. IST, after closing at 7.2365% on Thursday, headed for its biggest single-session rise since October 12. The yield is already up by 8 basis points for the week.

New Delhi is due to raise 330 billion rupees ($3.57 billion) through a bond sale later in the day.

"Oil (price) remains the key risk for the bond market and if it stays high, it will add to more selling pressure on bonds in the run-up to Reserve Bank of India's decision," a trader with a state-run bank said.

The benchmark Brent crude contract held above $96 a barrel in Asian trading, as fresh escalation in the Middle East conflict renewed fears that supply routes could be disrupted.

For India, the rise in crude prices is a significant macroeconomic concern, as the country is one of the world's largest oil importers. More expensive crude can put pressure on its current-account deficit, the rupee and add to already heightened inflation pressures.

Investor sentiment was also dampened after the RBI said food-price pressures remained broad-based and pointed to a "higher generalisation of price pressures" across the economy.

The comments come after India's retail inflation rose above the RBI's upper tolerance threshold of 6% in October, increasing pressure on policymakers to maintain a hawkish bias at their December 4 meeting.

A majority of economists polled by Reuters expect a 25-basis-point rate increase. Some market participants see scope for a larger move, as indicated by overnight index swaps and treasury bill yields.

RATES

OIS rates climbed 4-6 basis points across major points of the curve, tracking bond yields.

The one-year rate (INR1YMIBROIS=CC) was at 6.57%, while the two-year rate (INR2YIBROIS=CC) was at 6.51% and the liquid five-year rate (INR5YMIBROIS=CC) was at 6.50%.

($1 = 92.4450 Indian rupees)

data.title: Queen's Road Capital Announces Continuation of the NCIB
data.description:
Hong Kong, Hong Kong--(Newsfile Corp. - November 26, 2026) - Queen's Road Capital Investment Ltd. (the "Company" or "QRC") is pleased to announce that the Board of Directors of the Company has approved the continuation of the Company's normal course issuer bid for a further period of 12 months (the "2026 NCIB"). The Company's notice to commence the 2026 NCIB has been approved by the Toronto Stock Exchange (the "TSX").

The Company intends to purchase up to 1,760,000 common shares of the Company ("Common Shares") under the 2026 NCIB, representing approximately 3.26% of the Company's 54,048,082 issued and outstanding Common Shares as of November 19, 2026. Any shares purchased under the 2026 NCIB will be cancelled and returned to treasury. Purchases under the 2026 NCIB will be made through the facilities of the TSX and alternative trading systems in Canada. The NCIB enables the Company to repurchase its Common Shares for cancellation when the market price of its Common Shares may not fully reflect the underlying value of the Company's business and future prospects.

Any purchases under the 2026 NCIB will depend on future market conditions. The Company will determine the timing, amount and acceptable price of any such 2026 NCIB purchases, subject at all times to applicable TSX and other regulatory requirements. The period during which the Company is authorized to make purchases under the 2026 NCIB will commence on December 1, 2026, and will end 12 months thereafter on November 30, 2027, or such earlier date on which the maximum number of Common Shares is purchased under the 2026 NCIB or the 2026 NCIB is terminated at the Company's election. There are no assurances that any shares will be purchased under the 2026 NCIB, as purchases will depend on market conditions satisfactory to the Company during the term of the 2026 NCIB.

Under TSX rules, no more than 1,227 Common Shares (being 25% of the average daily trading volume on the TSX of 4,910 Common Shares for the six months May 1, 2026 to October 31, 2026) can be purchased on the TSX on any single trading day under the 2026 NCIB, with the exception that one block purchase in excess of the daily maximum is permitted per calendar week.

The 2026 NCIB continues the share purchase program approved by the Board of Directors on November 14, 2025 (the "2025 NCIB"). Under the 2025 NCIB, the Company purchased 658,900 Common Shares for total consideration of approximately C$9.0 million at a volume-weighted average price of C$13.68 per share through the facilities of the TSX and alternative trading systems in Canada. The Company was authorized to purchase 1,760,000 Common Shares under the 2025 NCIB.

QRC is a dividend paying, leading financier to the global resource sector. The Company is a resource focused investment company, making investments in privately held and publicly traded companies. The Company acquires and holds securities for long-term capital appreciation, with a focus on convertible debt securities and resource projects in advanced development or production located in politically safe jurisdictions.

data.title: Mahanadi Coalfields Listing: Coal India subsidiary debuts at a small discount to issue price
data.description:
Shares of Mahanadi Coalfields Ltd (MCL) listed on the stock exchanges on Friday, November 27, at a minor discount in comparison to the issue price. The shares began trading at ₹134 apiece compared to the issue price of ₹136 apiece.

The Mahanadi Coalfields Ltd. initial public offering (IPO) was oversubscribed by 1.52 times compared to the total number of shares on offer. The issue was a complete OFS, which means the company did not receive any proceeds from the transacton.

Mahanadi Coalfields' offer for sale comprised of 66.18 crore equity shares at ₹136 per share totaling ₹9,000 crore. Promoter Coal India is offloading 10% of its stake. Post the listing, the company's market cap is likely to be ₹90,000 crore.

The issue valued Mahanadi Coalfields at 8 times to 8.4 times its financial year 2026 Earnings per Share (EPS), which stood at ₹16.13.

Mahanadi Coalfields accounts for 21% of the total domestic coal production in India and 28.4% of Coal India's total coal production. The company's coal dispatch between financial year 2021-2026 grew at a Compounded Annual Growth Rate (CAGR) of 7.6%, while its Coal production grew at a 8.08% CAGR.

In FY26, its dispatches stood at 210.74 MT, while production stood at 218.31 MT. This is in comparison to the financial year 2025 and 2024 dispatches figures of 210.46 MT and 199.02 MT respectively, while production figures in the last two years stood at 225.17 MT and 206.1 MT.

Mahanadi Coalfield reported a revenue of ₹15,868.27 crore in the first half of FY27 while in the first quarter of FY26 its revenue was ₹14,398.8 crore.

The company's revenue in FY26 was at ₹29,854 crore compared to ₹30,483 crore in FY25 and ₹31,210 crore in FY24. Its margins expanded to 47.45% in FY26 from 46.42% in the year-ago period but were lower than FY24's 49.53%.

Here's why Mahanadi Coalfields is well-placed as an enterprise:

  • Favourable rail-led evacuation network complemented by port connectivity.
  • Highest surface production which helps in lowest cost of production per tonne.
  • Mahanadi Coalfields has the lowest stripping ratio of 1:1 while others are at 4:1.

The Mahanadi Coalfilds management spoke to CNBC-TV18 about demand, washery capacity, capex and more. Here are the key takeaways:

  • Incremental coal demand is of 600 MT in India which gives the company an opportunity to grow.
  • Washed coal demands 400 per tonne are better for profitability in comparison to the current numbers.
  • The MCL Washery capacity is expected to move to 37 MT in three to four years compared to the current 10 years.
  • E-auction volumes will account for approximately 18% of sales mix.
  • Capex is approximately ₹3,000 crore per year, which will be funded by internal accruals.
  • Intends to continue paying out healthy dividend.

data.title: China's Factory Activity Gauge Likely to Signal Improvement in November — Market Talk
data.description: The gauge for China's factory activity is likely to indicate improvement in November, according to Goldman Sachs in a research note. GS expects official manufacturing purchasing managers' index to edge up to 49.5 in November from 49.3 in October. A PMI reading below 50 signals contraction in activity. The improvement is supported by high-frequency indicators, such as steel production, which rose sequentially during the month, the bank says. It also expects the RatingDog manufacturing PMI, compiled by S&P Global, to rise to 52.2 in November from 52.0 in October, supported by stronger port activity in coastal regions compared with last month. data.title: China Shenhua raises $860 million in Hong Kong share sale to repay debt
data.description:
By Yantoultra Ngui

China Shenhua Energy , a Chinese coal producer, said on Friday it raised HK$6.74 billion ($860 million) in a Hong Kong share sale, mainly to repay debt in mainland China.

  • Reuters reported on Thursday, citing a term sheet, that China Shenhua , which is also listed on the Shanghai stock exchange, was seeking to raise up to $881 million by selling 177 million shares at HK$38.00 to HK$39.00 each

  • China Shenhua said in a filing that it would sell up to 177 million new Hong Kong shares at HK$38.10 each. The final price was 7.7% below the stock's HK$41.28 close on Thursday

  • China Shenhua plans to use about 90% of the proceeds to repay debts in mainland China and improve its funding structure. It plans to use the remaining 10% for general corporate purposes

  • The new shares represent about 0.82% of the company's existing outstanding shares, or 0.81% after the sale

  • Shares of China Shenhua dropped 6.5% to HK$38.58 on Friday, while its Shanghai shares declined 5.2%

($1 = 7.8364 Hong Kong dollars)

data.title: Indian central bank lets rupee rise to break one-way bets on depreciation
data.description:
By Nimesh Vora and Ira Dugal

India's central bank is using the return of foreign inflows to break bets on a one-way slide in the rupee, allowing the currency to strengthen rather than buying dollars to rebuild reserves.

The strategy could encourage exporters to sell more dollars, reduce hedging by importers and ease foreign investors' concerns over currency losses, analysts and two sources familiar with the Reserve Bank of India's thinking said.

Indian equities have drawn a record $16 billion in foreign inflows in November, reversing nearly two years of selling and providing the central bank an opportunity to rebuild reserves.

Yet, the RBI has largely stayed out of the currency market despite an $80 billion drawdown in reserves from their $785.7 billion peak, following heavy dollar sales in October to defend the rupee as it approached its record low of 96.96 per dollar.

The RBI's dollar purchases during the rupee's recovery have been limited despite around $40 billion in forward commitments maturing over the next year, Dhiraj Nim, FX strategist and senior economist at ANZ Bank, said.

"We think its immediate priority is to put exporter hedging on a sustained footing and ease forward market imbalances (between importer and exporter hedging)," he added.

"That may require further rupee appreciation."

Nim said the rupee would face stiff resistance at 90-91 per dollar. The currency traded at 92.62 on Friday.

The RBI is in "no hurry" to rebuild reserves and could allow the rupee to appreciate while replenishing reserves if inflows persist, one of the sources said, requesting anonymity due to restrictions on speaking to the media.

The strategy is consistent with Governor Sanjay Malhotra's publicly stated view that the rupee was undervalued.

An RBI spokesperson did not respond to an email seeking comment on the currency strategy.

EARLY SIGNS OF RESET

The rupee fell 4.8% in 2025 and another 5.5% in the first 10 months of this year, pressured by nearly $50 billion in foreign equity outflows amid India's limited exposure to the AI investment boom and steep valuations.

Persistent weakness prompted foreign investors to build short rupee positions in the offshore non-deliverable forwards market, exporters to retain dollar earnings and importers to step up hedging.

The resulting spiral prompted the RBI to curb open currency positions, impose reserve requirements on large hedging transactions and allow oil companies to buy dollars directly from its reserves.

With the rupee now up more than 4% from its lows, expectations are shifting.

Exporter hedging volumes over the past week were significantly higher than levels seen throughout the year, the head of markets at a large private-sector bank said, citing renewed hedging of future dollar receivables by Indian IT companies.

Investors turned bullish on the rupee for the first time in 18 months, helped by record foreign equity inflows and lower oil prices, a Reuters poll showed on Thursday.

FLEXIBILITY ON RATES

A sustained recovery in the rupee would provide the RBI higher flexibility to focus monetary policy on domestic growth and inflation conditions, rather than having to contend with currency weakness. This, in turn, could strengthen the rupee's fundamental support.

"Credible moves" on interest rates to address domestic sources of inflation would do more to ease underlying pressures on the rupee, said Aaron Hurd, senior portfolio manager for currency at State Street Investment Management.

"We need to see 2-3 more rate hikes over the coming quarters, preferably front-loaded with a hike at each of the next two meetings."
